report.releaseDate: 20 Oct 2026 (NBA Q2 2026 Financial Results & Quantitative Data; report PDF dated 27 Oct 2026)
report.currency: EUR (tables in € millions unless stated; ~USD at EUR/USD 1.1394, ECB reference rate 30 Jun 2026)
report.verdict: Cyprus's licensed betting market posted its strongest quarter in the NBA's published series in Q2 2026: GGR +23.6% YoY to €46.9m (~$53.4m) on stakes of €329.8m (~$375.8m, +10.6%), a series-high 14.2% hold, and online (Class B) now 64% of GGR. The regime is narrow (sports betting only; online casino, slots and exchanges prohibited), fiscally stable (15% of GGR all-in; 19 licensees unchanged for six quarters) and tightening at the edges — B2B supplier licensing, retail self-exclusion and social-media advertising enforcement are the live files, tax is not. For an operator the prize is a c.€120m-a-year online GGR pool contested by 13 incumbents; for a technology supplier the coming B2B licence is the more consequential change.
summary: **Record quarter for regulated betting.** The National Betting Authority (NBA) reports Q2 2026 (Apr–Jun) stakes of €329,816,209 (~$375.8m), +10.6% YoY vs €298.1m, and GGR (stakes minus winnings, before tax) of €46,882,290 (~$53.4m), +23.6% YoY vs €37.9m — the highest quarterly GGR in the series published since 2023. Winnings paid were €282.9m (~$322.4m, +8.8%).

**Read the headline carefully — €329.8m is stakes, not revenue.** The NBA labels pay-in as 'comprehensive income' (and in its abstract 'gross gaming revenue (pay in)') and calls true GGR 'net gambling revenue'. Trade-press headlines of 'sports betting grows 11% to €329.8m' therefore describe turnover; the revenue pool is €46.9m a quarter, c.€185m annualised.

**Hold, not volume, drove the beat.** Blended hold rose to 14.2% from 12.7% a year earlier and 12.7% in Q1-26 — the highest in the 2023–26 series (prior peak 14.1% in Q4-24). Class A (retail) hold hit 21.5% (19.2% Q2-25); Class B (online) 12.0% (10.6%). Stakes fell 8.4% QoQ, in line with normal Q1→Q2 seasonality (−7.1% in 2025, −10.5% in 2024) despite the FIFA World Cup starting 11 June.

**Online is two-thirds of the market and compounding faster.** Class B stakes €252.3m (~$287.5m, +12.6% YoY) and GGR €30.2m (~$34.4m, +27.2%); Class A stakes €77.5m (~$88.3m, +4.9%) and GGR €16.7m (~$19.0m, +17.5%). Online took 76.5% of stakes (75.2% a year ago) and 64.4% of GGR (62.6%). FY2025 online GGR was €99.7m (~$113.6m, 61.6% of the total).

**FY2025 base and trend.** Full-year 2025 stakes €1,327.0m (~$1,512m, +8.4% vs 2024 €1,224.6m); GGR €161.8m (~$184.4m, +2.6% vs €157.7m) as hold normalised to 12.2% from 12.9%; levies €24.3m (~$27.7m: tax €16.2m + contribution €8.1m). 2026 is re-accelerating: H1 GGR growth of 16.8% vs +2.6% for FY2025. NBA chair Trisokkas has publicly framed 2025 as '>€1.3bn turnover, +8%'.

**Regulator and law.** The NBA (Εθνική Αρχή Στοιχημάτων) licenses and supervises betting under the Betting Law of 2019, L.37(I)/2019, as amended (most recently by L.162(I)/2024). Two licence classes: Class A (land-based betting in licensed premises, excluding horse racing) and Class B (online betting). Class B explicitly excludes slot machines, online casino games and electronic horse-racing; exchange betting, spread betting and RNG casino products are not licensable. Online casino remains prohibited — there is no liberalisation signal.

**Tax: 15% of GGR, all-in, base = net proceeds (X − Y).** Betting tax of 10% of net betting proceeds is paid to the Republic and a contribution of 5% to the NBA (per Directive 14.2025.v2: 4% + 1%; the 4% is routed to the Cyprus Sports Organisation/KOA for sport, the 1% to youth protection and gambling-harm programmes). The contribution rose from 3% to 5% effective 30 Dec 2024 (L.162(I)/2024). Note: press coverage at bill stage (Dec 2024) reported 4.5%; the regulator's data and directive show 5% — we use the regulator figure. Payment is monthly, by end of the following month. Free bets/bonuses are treated as stakes when placed (s.74(7)), so promo-led acquisition is taxed.

**Licensing is cheap on fees but capital-heavy.** Class A or B licence: €30,000 (~$34.2k) for one year or €45,000 (~$51.3k) for two (Betting (Payable Fees) Regulations, R.A.A. 84/2019). Authorised-agent and additional-premises licences €2,000/€3,000 (first premises free; €170/month pro-rata). Applicants need €500,000 (~$0.57m) paid-up share capital, a €550,000 (~$0.63m) bank guarantee from a Cyprus/EU credit institution valid six months past expiry, a Cyprus company or registered branch with betting as principal activity, a .com.cy domain and a backup server in the Republic (capital/guarantee/server details from law-firm summaries, consistent across sources).

**Operator landscape: 13 online, 6 retail, no published shares.** Class B register (Q2-26): bet365 (Hillside New Media Cyprus, B001), Bet on Alfa (B005), Meridianbet (B009), UBET (B008), Megabetplus/Scorebet (Cleverpath, B011), Winmasters (Level Up Interactive, B004), Fonbet (Fortune Entertainment RG, B012), Allwynbet (OPAP Sports, B017), Stoiximan (B018), IN2BET (I.T.S., B016), Cybet (Betathlon, B021), Novibet (Gamart, B022; licensed Sep 2025) and CopyBet (B020). Class A: Betathlon/Cybet, Bet on Alfa, OPAP Sports/Allwynbet, Meridian, Cleverpath/Megabetplus and Bookieco. Class B count peaked at 14 (Q2–Q3 2024) and has been 13 since Q4-24; Class A fell from 7 to 6 in Q1-24. The NBA publishes no per-operator GGR, so market shares are n/a.

**Retail is a 461-shop, agent-led network that is still growing GGR.** Premises: Nicosia 162, Limassol 134, Larnaca 83, Paphos 46, Famagusta 36 (total +1 YoY, +2 QoQ). 338 authorised agents vs only 87 bookmaker-owned shops (−8% YoY) — a franchise model. Persons-in-charge 1,375 (+10%) and total employees 1,584 (+10.3%). Licence cancellations/withdrawals 8 in Q2 (+167% YoY off a base of 3). Average GGR per premises €36.2k (~$41k) per quarter vs €30.8k a year ago.

**Casino is a separate, monopoly regime.** The Cyprus Gaming and Casino Supervision Commission (CGC) regulates Melco's single 30-year licence (granted 2017) with 15-year exclusivity to 2032 and a 15% gaming duty on GGR that cannot be raised during exclusivity. CGC-reported casino GGR: €130m (2023) → €189m (2024, ~$215m) → €227m (2025, ~$258.6m, +20.1%), with City of Dreams Mediterranean (Limassol, opened Jul 2023) 86% of 2025. Melco's Q2-26 Cyprus revenue was US$82.0m (vs $72.3m, +13.4%) with Adjusted EBITDA US$19.9m (vs $12.4m, +60%); Melco now cites three satellite casinos (Larnaca site reported closed — secondary source).

**Lottery/numerical games sit with OPAP Cyprus.** OPAP (Allwyn) holds a 15-year exclusive concession (signed mid-2024) for designated games of chance (Joker, Lotto, Proto, Kino, Super 3, Extra 5, Propo, Propogoal) paying 22.5% of GGR in tax plus 5% of GGR in sponsorship; Cyprus was c.7% of OPAP group GGR in H1 2024 (Edison). Cyprus-specific lottery GGR is not published — n/a; a rough cross-check (7% × OPAP FY2025 group GGR €2,408m ≈ €170m) is an estimate only. Combined betting + casino GGR for 2025 was €388.8m (~$443m), excluding lottery.

**Payments are card/bank-rail only.** Class B accounts may be funded only by bank transfer, debit/credit card or e-money from an authorised issuer; cash and crypto are not permitted; client funds must sit in segregated Cyprus bank accounts with no set-off; retail is cash. Cyprus is a card/bank economy — mobile-money considerations do not apply. Withdrawal within five working days is cited by secondary sources [unverified against the law text].

**Responsible gambling is moving from online to omnichannel.** A national online self-exclusion platform has operated since Feb 2024; the NBA's 2026–2028 strategic plan seeks to extend self-exclusion to betting shops, strengthen treatment programmes and support vulnerable groups. An NBA survey (Jul 2026, n=1,000, ages 18–35) found 93% saw gambling content on social media, 89% paid betting/online-casino ads and 77% influencer promotions. Problem-gambling prevalence is cited at c.3% by the NBA chair (secondary report; methodology unverified). The 9th Safer Gambling Week ran 12–18 Oct 2026.

**Enforcement is blocking-led and escalating.** The ISP blocking list reached 22,660 domains at end-June 2026 (+245 in Q2, +406 in Q1, +4.7% YoY; 2,638 in Q1-2017). Participation in illegal gambling carries up to one year's imprisonment/€50,000 (~$57k) fine; operating unlicensed gambling up to five years/€300,000 (~$342k); administrative fines up to €100,000 (~$114k) per finding [secondary]. The NBA has announced plans to gain powers against illegal promotions on social media, apps and search platforms and is lobbying for EU-level cooperation.

**Political direction: protect, don't liberalise; license the supply chain.** Finance Minister Keravnos (9th Safer Gambling Conference, 12 Oct 2026) stressed growth 'cannot be assessed solely on economic indicators'. The NBA has drafted a bill (flagged Nov 2025, detailed Aug 2026) introducing a first-ever B2B supplier licensing regime and 'legal inclusion of new products' — the latter undefined; nothing indicates online casino. A proposal to restrict gambling by Guaranteed Minimum Income recipients surfaced in Sep 2026 [details unverified]. Parliament showed in Dec 2024 it will raise betting levies to fund football — a ratchet precedent.

**Read-through for B2Tech.** As a B2C entrant: addressable regulated online GGR is c.€120–125m annualised (H1-26 €59.9m), split among 13 licensees led by Greek-market brands (Stoiximan, Novibet, Allwynbet/OPAP) and bet365; entry requires c.€1.05m of committed capital/guarantee plus €30k fee, a .com.cy site, local server and Greek-language product, with 15% GGR levy, promo taxation and no casino cross-sell. As a B2B platform/feed supplier: the coming supplier licence makes Cyprus a formal EU credential and a compliance obligation — engage early in the consultation.

**Data caveats.** All betting figures are regulator-reported and gross of tax; casino figures are from Melco (company) and a CGC report relayed by press; lottery GGR, per-operator shares, advertising-code content and the GMI proposal text could not be verified from primary documents.

segments.name: Online betting (Class B)
segments.headline: Online GGR +27% YoY to €30.2m on a 12.0% hold; 13 licensees unchanged, 64% of market GGR and still gaining share.
narrative: Class B bookmakers took €252,309,661 (~$287.5m) in stakes in Q2 2026, +12.6% on Q2 2025 (€224.2m) and +19% on Q2 2024, and paid out €222,098,789 (~$253.1m) in winnings, leaving GGR of €30,210,872 (~$34.4m), +27.2% YoY. Stakes fell 7.6% QoQ from Q1's €273.0m, but GGR edged up 1.8% because hold improved to 12.0% from 10.9% in Q1 and 10.6% a year earlier. The online hold series (9–12% since 2023) shows this is the top of the historical range; FY2025 online hold was 10.0%, so roughly a fifth of the Q2 GGR growth is results/mix rather than volume. Betting tax on the segment was €3.02m (~$3.4m) and the 5% contribution €1.51m (~$1.7m).

On a half-year basis online stakes were €525.3m (~$598.5m, +14.9%) and GGR €59.9m (~$68.2m, +23.9%), implying a 2026 run-rate of roughly €120–125m of regulated online GGR against €99.7m in FY2025 (+4.9% that year) and €95.0m in FY2024. Online's share of market GGR has moved from 55.8% (FY2023) to 60.3% (FY2024), 61.6% (FY2025) and 64.6% in H1 2026; by stakes it is 76%. The segment's growth is therefore structural channel shift plus hold, not a one-quarter event.

The supply side is static: 13 Class B licensees every quarter since Q4 2024 (12 in Q1 2023, peak 14 in Q2–Q3 2024). Average GGR per licensee is c.€2.3m (~$2.6m) per quarter, but the distribution is almost certainly highly skewed toward the Greek-market brands — Stoiximan (title sponsor of the Cypriot First Division, 'Cyprus League by Stoiximan'), Novibet (licensed Sep 2025), Allwynbet (OPAP Sports; the former OPAP betting brand) — and bet365, with Fonbet, Meridianbet, Winmasters, Bet on Alfa, UBET, Megabetplus/Scorebet, IN2BET, Cybet and CopyBet behind. The NBA publishes no per-operator data, so shares are n/a; any third-party share estimate should be treated as unverified. Five of the 13 also hold Class A licences (Betathlon/Cybet, Bet on Alfa, OPAP Sports, Meridian, Cleverpath), giving them omnichannel wallets and shop-based cash-in that pure online entrants lack.

Product scope is the binding constraint. A Class B licence covers bets on sports events and 'other events in which natural persons participate' at bookmaker-set odds; it excludes slot machines, online casino games and electronic horse-racing, and exchange, spread and RNG products are not licensable. There is no legal online casino in Cyprus and the 2026 reform bill, while referencing 'legal inclusion of new products', has given no indication that casino is in scope. Operators must trade on a .com.cy domain, run a backup server in the Republic connected in parallel to the main server, and can only take funds via bank transfer, cards or authorised e-money — no cash, no crypto. The NBA's youth survey (89% of 18–35s saw paid online-casino advertising) is a reminder that demand for casino exists and leaks offshore, which is also why the blocking list keeps growing.

Licence renewals are a near-term watch item: bet365 (B001) and Allwynbet (B017) expire 31 Dec 2026; Bet on Alfa (B005) 23 Jan 2027; Stoiximan (B018) 30 Jan 2027; IN2BET (B016) 9 Feb 2027; Cybet (B021) 8 Mar 2027; Meridian (B009) 19 Mar 2027. Renewal is routine (two-year terms at €45,000), but it is the natural point for the NBA to impose new conditions (self-exclusion integration, advertising undertakings, B2B supplier disclosure). Commercially, Q2 2026 captured only the first ~20 days of the FIFA World Cup (11 Jun–19 Jul); the Q3 2026 print, due around January 2027, will show the full tournament effect and whether hold normalises toward 10–11%.

Implication for an entrant: the regulated online pool is real and growing double-digit, but it is small (c.€30m a quarter), Greek-language, incumbent-dense and promo-taxed (free bets count as stakes under s.74(7)). A credible plan needs a differentiated sportsbook (pricing, in-play, local football depth), a retail or payments partnership for cash-in, and acceptance that there is no casino margin to subsidise acquisition. Marketing intensity is unquantified in regulator data (no spend disclosure).

segments.name: Retail betting (Class A)
segments.headline: Retail GGR +17.5% to €16.7m on a 21.5% hold with a flat 461-shop estate — an agent-led network that is monetising better, not expanding.
narrative: Six Class A bookmakers took €77,506,547 (~$88.3m) in stakes in Q2 2026 (+4.9% YoY; +2% vs Q2 2024) and paid out €60,835,130 (~$69.3m), for GGR of €16,671,417 (~$19.0m), +17.5% YoY and +2.9% QoQ. The retail hold of 21.5% is the highest in the published series (18–21% range since 2023; 19.2% in Q2 2025; 18.6% in Q1 2026), consistent with a parlay-heavy shop product and, in this quarter, favourable results. H1 2026 retail stakes were €164.6m (~$187.5m, +1.8%) and GGR €32.9m (~$37.5m, +5.7%); FY2025 retail GGR was €62.1m (~$70.8m, −0.9%), so retail is a low-single-digit volume business whose GGR swings with hold.

The estate is stable and agent-operated. Licensed premises numbered 461 at end-June (459 in Q1-26; 460 in Q2-25; 494 in Q2-23), split Nicosia 162 (−1% YoY), Limassol 134 (+3%), Larnaca 83 (−1%), Paphos 46 (−4%) and Famagusta 36 (+3%). Only 87 premises are operated directly by Class A bookmakers (−8% YoY from 95), versus 338 licensed authorised agents (natural and legal persons) running the remainder — the franchise/agent model dominates and keeps bookmaker capex low. Persons in charge of premises rose 10% to 1,375 and total employment 10.3% to 1,584, implying rising staffing per shop rather than more shops. Licence cancellations/withdrawals were 8 in Q2 (18 in Q1; 3 in Q2-25).

Unit economics at the regulator level: GGR per premises was c.€36.2k (~$41k) in the quarter (€30.8k a year earlier), or c.€145k annualised, before the 15% levy, agent commission (reported to the NBA in Annex A but not published), staff and rent. The Class A licence excludes horse-racing (run separately by the Nicosia Race Club) and any Class B services; shops cannot host casino or machine gaming. Premises licences are cheap (€2,000/year beyond the first, pro-rated at €170/month to the bookmaker's licence term) and Class A operators must file per-premises pay-in/pay-out/offer statements monthly.

Direction of travel is toward tighter retail player protection rather than expansion: the NBA's 2026–2028 strategic plan proposes extending the national self-exclusion scheme (online-only since Feb 2024) to betting shops, which will require identification at point-of-bet or at least at pay-out, and the Sep 2026 proposal on Guaranteed Minimum Income recipients, if enacted, would add eligibility checks. Both raise the fixed-cost base for an agent network of 461 outlets. For an entrant the retail route is not about building shops; it is about whether a partnership with one of the six Class A licensees or their agents can provide cash deposit/withdrawal points for an online brand, as the five dual-licensed incumbents already enjoy.

segments.name: Licensing, tax & operator landscape
segments.headline: A low-fee, capital-gated, GGR-taxed regime at 15% all-in, stable since the Dec 2024 levy rise — with B2B supplier licensing the next structural change.
narrative: The Betting Law of 2019 (L.37(I)/2019), which replaced the 2012 Act, vests licensing, supervision, tax collection and enforcement in the National Betting Authority. Licences are issued for one or two years (fees €30,000 / €45,000, ~$34k / ~$51k) to a company limited by shares incorporated in Cyprus or an overseas company with a Cyprus branch whose principal activity is betting; fit-and-proper tests cover directors, UBOs and key persons. Financial gates are €500,000 (~$0.57m) of issued and paid-up capital plus a €550,000 (~$0.63m) bank guarantee from a Cyprus or EU credit institution, valid for six months after licence expiry, from which unpaid tax outstanding more than 60 days can be recovered. Refused applicants get 75% of the fee back (s.31). Audited accounts and an annual report are due by 30 June (s.71). Administrative fines of up to €100,000 (~$114k) per finding are cited by secondary sources. There is no numerical cap on Class B licences and no local-ownership requirement; localisation is via the Cyprus entity, .com.cy domain and in-country backup server.

Tax is levied on net betting proceeds — 'X' (all amounts paid to the bookmaker for bets in the period) minus 'Y' (winnings paid, including returned/void stakes and amounts withdrawable on demand) — at 10% to the Republic as betting tax and 5% to the NBA as contribution, for an all-in 15% of GGR; there is no turnover tax and the NBA data show no player-level withholding (whether winnings are taxed in the player's hands was not verified here). Two features matter for modelling: (i) under s.74(7) a bet placed with a free bet or discounted stake is deemed to have been paid in full, so promotions are inside the tax base; and (ii) the contribution was lifted from 3% to 5% with effect from 30 December 2024 by L.162(I)/2024, a Finance-Ministry bill passed 27 votes to a contested minority specifically to double the slice flowing via the Cyprus Sports Organisation to the football federation (from 1.5% to 3% of net proceeds). Directive 14.2025.v2 splits the 5% as 4% + 1%; the 4% funds sport (and an ethics committee) through KOA and the 1% youth-protection/harm programmes. Press at bill stage reported the rate as 4.5%; the enacted and applied rate is 5%.

Fiscal yield is modest but rising: FY2025 betting tax €16.2m (~$18.5m) and contribution €8.1m (~$9.2m) = €24.3m (~$27.7m); H1 2026 €13.9m (~$15.9m, +16.8%). On current trends FY2026 levies would be c.€27–28m (estimate). Set against the casino's 15% duty on €227m of 2025 GGR (implied c.€34m, estimate) and OPAP Cyprus's 22.5% + 5%, betting is the lightest-taxed vertical in Cyprus — which is precisely why it was the target of the 2024 increase and why the contribution, rather than the headline 10%, is the lever most exposed to future political demands (sport funding, treatment programmes).

The operator roster is mature and consolidated. Of 19 licensees, five hold both classes (Betathlon/Cybet, Bet on Alfa, OPAP Sports/Allwynbet, Meridian, Cleverpath/Megabetplus), one is retail-only (Bookieco, licensed Feb 2026) and eight are online-only (bet365, UBET, Winmasters, Fonbet, Stoiximan, IN2BET, Novibet, CopyBet). The newest online entrant is Novibet (Sep 2025); the most recent renewals were UBET (Apr 2026), Winmasters (May 2026) and CopyBet (Jun 2026). The NBA has not disclosed any operator's GGR, so leadership claims are inference: the Greek-facing scale brands (Stoiximan, Novibet, Allwynbet) and bet365 are the obvious candidates. The static licensee count since Q4 2024 alongside +27% online GGR growth suggests incumbents are capturing the growth, not new entrants.

The next structural change is supply-side. In Nov 2025 and again in Aug 2026 the NBA chair said a new bill has been drafted that takes 'a more holistic approach' to unlicensed activity, introduces a dedicated licensing regime for B2B platform, software and service suppliers — described as 'long overdue' given the density of gaming-technology companies headquartered in Cyprus — and provides for the legal inclusion of new (betting) products. For a technology company this is the single most relevant Cyprus development: it converts an informal hub into a licensed one, with ownership, governance and activity disclosure, and will likely require Class B operators to source only from licensed suppliers. Timing is not fixed; the bill has not yet been tabled in the House as far as the public record shows.

segments.name: Casino, lottery & adjacent verticals
segments.headline: Casino GGR €227m in 2025 (+20%) under Melco's exclusive licence; Q2-26 Cyprus revenue US$82m (+13%) and EBITDA +60%; lottery sits with OPAP Cyprus on a 15-year exclusive — neither is contestable before 2032.
narrative: Land-based casino gaming is regulated by the Cyprus Gaming and Casino Supervision Commission (CGC), established in 2017, under a framework designed for a single integrated casino resort: one 30-year licence (renewable from year 12), 15 years of exclusivity from grant (2017, hence to 2032) during which no other casino licence may be issued, and a gaming duty of 15% of GGR with no deductions other than a free-play allowance, which cannot be raised during the exclusivity period. Melco (through ICR Cyprus, 75% Melco / 25% Cyprus Phassouri) opened City of Dreams Mediterranean in Zakaki, Limassol in July 2023 after operating a temporary casino, and was permitted up to four satellite casinos (Nicosia, Larnaca, Paphos, Ayia Napa). Melco's Q2 2026 release refers to 'three satellite casinos'; a secondary source indicates the Larnaca site has closed [unverified against CGC].

A CGC report delivered to the Presidency (relayed by press, Apr 2026) puts casino GGR at €130m (~$148m) in 2023, €189m (~$215m) in 2024 and €227m (~$258.6m) in 2025, +20.1%, with the Limassol resort generating 86% of 2025 GGR. At 15%, implied 2025 duty is c.€34m (~$39m) — an estimate; the CGC's own tax-take figure was not located. Casino GGR is therefore c.1.4x licensed betting GGR, and the combined regulated betting + casino pool in 2025 was €388.8m (~$443m), before lottery. Melco's company data for Q2 2026 show Cyprus ('City of Dreams Mediterranean and Other') revenue of US$82.0m vs US$72.3m (+13.4%) and Adjusted EBITDA of US$19.9m vs US$12.4m (+60%), with management attributing the rebound to easing Middle-East travel disruption — i.e. the casino is tourism-geared, whereas betting is domestic.

Lottery and numerical games are reserved to OPAP Cyprus, present since 1969 under a Greece–Cyprus intergovernmental arrangement and, since mid-2024, under a 15-year exclusive concession with the Republic for designated games of chance (Joker, Lotto, Proto, Kino, Super 3, Extra 5, Propo, Propogoal). OPAP pays 22.5% of GGR in tax plus 5% of GGR for sporting, social and charitable sponsorship, and a concession fee payable in annual instalments (amount not verified). Cyprus-specific GGR is not disclosed in the sources read; Edison put Cyprus at c.7% of OPAP group GGR in H1 2024, which against OPAP's FY2025 group GGR of €2,407.9m would imply very roughly €170m — an estimate only and not a regulator figure. OPAP's betting arm in Cyprus trades as Allwynbet under NBA Class A and B licences, so the lottery incumbent is also a full betting competitor.

The implication is that the only contestable vertical in Cyprus is sports betting. Casino (land-based) is locked until at least 2032, online casino is illegal, and lottery/numerical games are exclusive until 2039. An operator cannot bundle casino with sportsbook in Cyprus, and the typical European cross-sell economics do not apply; conversely, the casino monopoly means there is no licensed online competitor for casino-style spend, which keeps the offshore market (and the NBA's blocking list) large.

segments.name: Payments, responsible gambling, advertising & enforcement
segments.headline: Card/bank-rail-only payments, a 22,660-domain blocking list, a national self-exclusion scheme going omnichannel, and a regulator seeking social-media advertising powers — compliance cost is rising even as tax is flat.
narrative: Payments in Cyprus are conventional and tightly prescribed. Class B player accounts may be funded only from a bank account, by debit or credit card, by electronic transfer or with electronic money issued by an authorised issuer; cash is prohibited for online bets and cryptocurrency is not an accepted method, which is why no licensed .com.cy site offers crypto. Operators must hold player funds in segregated accounts at a Cyprus credit institution with written undertakings against set-off, may not accept a bet unless the player account holds sufficient cleared funds, and secondary sources cite a five-working-day pay-out requirement [unverified in the law text]. Retail betting is cash-based at the counter, which is the practical reason dual-licensed operators enjoy a cash-in advantage. Mobile money is not a feature of the market; Cyprus is a euro-area card and bank-transfer economy with instant SEPA widely available.

Responsible-gambling architecture is built around the NBA and its Safer Gambling programme (safergambling.gov.cy). A national self-exclusion platform launched on 20 February 2024 allows temporary or indefinite exclusion from all licensed online bookmakers via a single registration, with operators integrating by API and obliged to suppress marketing to excluded players; the 2026–2028 strategic plan commits to extending exclusion to land-based premises, strengthening treatment and rehabilitation (with the National Addictions Authority) and improving support for vulnerable groups, funded in part by the 1% harm-prevention slice of the contribution. The NBA's 2026 youth survey (1,000 respondents aged 18–35) found 93% exposure to gambling content on social media, 89% to paid betting/online-casino advertising and 77% to influencer promotions; the chair cites problem-gambling prevalence of around 3% (secondary report; survey methodology not verified). The 9th Safer Gambling Week (12–18 Oct 2026) was opened by the Finance Minister's message that growth 'cannot and must not be assessed solely on the basis of economic indicators' — the clearest signal of the political mood.

Advertising is governed by NBA codes and directives (a Code of Practice on Betting Advertising was consulted on in Feb 2019 under the predecessor law; the current directive text was not read for this note — content [unverified]). What is documented is intent: the NBA has announced plans to strengthen its powers over illegal gambling promotions on social media, mobile apps and search platforms, and the survey above is the evidence base. Separately, a proposal to restrict gambling by recipients of the Guaranteed Minimum Income surfaced in September 2026 [details unverified]. Expect tighter rules on influencer marketing, bonus advertising and platform-level takedowns within the 2026–28 plan horizon rather than an outright ad ban.

Enforcement rests on ISP blocking under ss.83–87 of the 2019 Law, in operation since 2015: the list stood at 22,660 domains at end-June 2026 (+245 in Q2, +406 in Q1, +4.7% YoY, from 2,638 in Q1 2017), published as a live text file. Sanctions cited by secondary sources are up to one year's imprisonment and/or a €50,000 (~$57k) fine for participating in illegal gambling and up to five years and/or €300,000 (~$342k) for providing it, with NBA administrative fines up to €100,000 (~$114k) per finding. The NBA chair has repeatedly called for EU-level coordination against offshore operators and for AI/data tools to detect illegal activity — a theme of the Oct 2026 conference. For a licensed operator the enforcement direction is supportive (channeling demand onshore); for a supplier it means that serving blocked operators into Cyprus will become a licensing issue once the B2B regime arrives.

highlights.text: Online GGR is compounding at +24–27% (Q2 +27.2%, H1 +23.9%) with a static 13-licensee base: the regulated online pool is c.€120–125m (~$137–142m) annualised vs €99.7m in FY2025, and online share of GGR has risen every year (55.8% FY23 → 64.6% H1-26). Growth is accruing to incumbents, which is the argument for entering via acquisition or partnership rather than greenfield.

Fiscal regime is predictable and GGR-based: 15% all-in (10% + 5%) on net proceeds, no turnover tax, monthly settlement, and no change signalled since the Dec 2024 rise. Betting is also the lightest-taxed vertical on the island (casino 15% + corporate, OPAP 22.5% + 5%), supporting mid-teens EBITDA margins for scaled operators.

Entry is cheap on fees and uncapped: €30,000/€45,000 (~$34k/$51k) licence, c.€1.05m (~$1.2m) capital + guarantee, two-year terms, no numerical cap and no local-ownership rule. The NBA has shown it will license new online brands (Novibet 2025, CopyBet, Fonbet) and retail entrants (Bookieco 2026).

Hold expansion shows pricing power: blended 14.2% (series high), retail 21.5%, online 12.0%. Even on a normalised 12–13% blended hold, stakes growth of 10–12% supports high-single to low-double-digit GGR growth.

Retail remains a cash-flow positive, agent-financed channel (+17.5% GGR, flat shops, employment +10%), and dual-licensed operators use 461 premises as cash-in/cash-out points — a partnership lever for an online entrant.

B2B supplier licensing (draft bill, 2025–26) would give platform, odds-feed and software providers a formal EU-regulated credential in a jurisdiction that already hosts a dense gaming-technology cluster; early engagement in the consultation is an opportunity for B2Tech as a supplier regardless of any B2C decision.

FIFA World Cup 2026 (11 Jun–19 Jul) falls mostly in Q3: only ~20 days sat in the record Q2, so the Q3 2026 print should show a further stakes step-up; the NBA itself has flagged a positive tournament effect.

lowlights.text: Product scope is sportsbook-only: no online casino, slots, poker, exchange, spread or RNG products are licensable, land-based casino is Melco-exclusive to 2032 and lottery is OPAP-exclusive to 2039. There is no casino cross-sell to fund acquisition, and offshore casino demand (89% of 18–35s saw online-casino ads; 22,660 blocked domains) will keep leaking.

Levy ratchet precedent: parliament raised the contribution from 3% to 5% in Dec 2024 explicitly to fund football clubs, over Finance-Committee dissent about rewarding indebted clubs. With sport and treatment funding both tied to betting GGR, further increments to the contribution are the most likely fiscal risk; the 10% betting tax itself looks stable.
Promotions are inside the tax base (s.74(7): free/discounted bets deemed paid in full), raising the effective levy on bonus-led acquisition well above 15% of cash GGR for promo-heavy entrants.

Hold is at a series high and will mean-revert: Q3 is seasonally the weakest-hold quarter (11.2% in Q3-25) and a return to a 12% blended hold would strip c.15% from GGR at constant stakes. Q2's +23.6% GGR growth overstates the underlying +10.6% stakes trend.

Incumbent density and opacity: 13 online licensees, five of them omnichannel, led by Greek-market scale brands (Stoiximan, Novibet, Allwynbet/OPAP) and bet365; the NBA publishes no operator shares, so an entrant cannot size the contestable share from public data and must model on inference.

Player-protection and advertising tightening is the policy direction: retail self-exclusion, social-media/app/search enforcement powers, possible restrictions on Guaranteed Minimum Income recipients and explicit ministerial messaging that growth is not the metric. These add compliance cost and constrain influencer/bonus marketing, the channels the NBA's own survey shows reach young adults.

Small absolute scale: €47m of quarterly GGR across 19 licensees (~€2.3m average per online licensee) means a sub-scale entrant carrying €1.05m of tied capital, a Cyprus entity, local server, Greek-language product and 15% levy needs a mid-single-digit share just to cover fixed compliance costs.

Nomenclature risk in the regulator's own data: the NBA labels stakes as 'comprehensive income' and even 'gross gaming revenue (pay in)' while calling GGR 'net gambling revenue'; press repeatedly reports the €330m–360m stakes figure as 'the market'. Internal sizing must be anchored on the €46.9m/quarter net-proceeds line.

forecast.intro: The base has moved. FY2025 licensed-betting GGR was €161.8m (~$184.4m), only +2.6% as hold normalised; H1 2026 delivered €92.8m (~$105.7m), +16.8%, with online (Class B) contributing €59.9m (+23.9%) and retail €32.9m (+5.7%). The second half carries the bulk of the FIFA World Cup (Q3) and the seasonally strongest Q4 (Q4-25 GGR €47.4m), offset by likely hold normalisation from Q2's 14.2% toward the 12–13% range. Regulatory moving parts — B2B supplier licensing, retail self-exclusion, social-media advertising powers, GMI-recipient restrictions — are compliance-cost events, not tax events; the 15% GGR levy has no announced change. Licensee count (6 + 13) is unlikely to move materially before the Dec 2026–Mar 2027 renewal cluster.

forecast.view: **Market:** we expect licensed betting GGR of **€183–189m in 2026 (+13–17%)** and a return to **high-single/low-double-digit growth in 2027** as hold normalises, with online passing **two-thirds of GGR** and retail flat-to-low-single-digit; stakes should exceed **€1.45bn** in 2026. The regulated online pool approaches **€130m by 2027** — meaningful for a regional operator, not for a global one. **Margin:** 15% all-in GGR levy is stable; the risk is a further contribution increment (sport/treatment funding) rather than a change to the 10% tax, and promo taxation keeps effective rates above headline for acquisition-led players. **Rules:** direction is protective and supply-side — expect the B2B supplier licensing bill to be tabled within 12 months, retail self-exclusion and social-media/app advertising powers within the 2026–28 plan, and no move to legalise online casino; casino exclusivity (2032) and the OPAP concession (2039) are not in play. **Enforcement** stays blocking-led with growing EU cooperation. **For B2Tech:** the B2C case is a share-take from 13 incumbents in a Greek-language, sportsbook-only market with c.€1.1m of tied capital and no casino margin — viable only with a differentiated product or an acquisition of an existing Class B licensee; the B2B case is stronger, because supplier licensing will formalise access to all 13 online operators and the technology cluster already on the island.
watch: Q3 2026 NBA release (c. Jan 2027): full World Cup effect on stakes and whether blended hold reverts below 13%; online share of GGR vs 64.4%.

Tabling and text of the NBA's reform bill: scope of B2B supplier licensing (fees, ownership disclosure, whether Class B operators must use licensed suppliers), and what 'new products' means (virtuals? pools? not casino).
Renewal cluster Dec 2026–Mar 2027: bet365 and Allwynbet (31 Dec 2026), Bet on Alfa, Stoiximan, IN2BET, Cybet, Meridian — any new conditions attached, and any net change to the 13-licensee count.
Advertising: issuance of social-media/app/search enforcement powers and any directive on influencer and bonus marketing following the 93%/89%/77% youth-exposure survey.
Retail self-exclusion rollout and the Guaranteed Minimum Income restriction proposal — operational cost for 461 premises and 338 agents.
Fiscal: any proposal to lift the 5% contribution again (sport or treatment funding) ahead of the 2027 budget; H1-26 levy run-rate €13.9m.
Casino/lottery adjacency: CGC annual GGR for 2026 (2025: €227m), Melco's satellite footprint, and OPAP/Allwynbet's omnichannel push into betting.
Blocking list growth (>22,660) and any EU-level cooperation mechanism the NBA secures against offshore casino operators targeting Cypriots.
